clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old boy presented with progressive vision loss, difficulty opening eyes, bilateral ptosis, and restricted eye movements, consistent with progressive external ophthalmoplegia. Ocular examination revealed pigmentary retinopathy with hyperpigmentation, visual field defects, and macular abnormalities. He also had a history of dizziness, fatigue, and growth retardation. Workup included a 24-hour ambulatory ECG, which showed intermittent first-degree atrioventricular block and partial second-degree type I atrioventricular block, indicating cardiac conduction abnormalities. Although genetic testing was performed and stated to support the diagnosis, the specific results were not disclosed. Other investigations for cerebellar ataxia and elevated CSF protein were either not reported or not found.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: 13-year-old boy with onset before age 20 years
Progressive external ophthalmoplegia manifested as difficulty opening eyes, bilateral ptosis, and restricted eye movements in all gaze directions

Pigmentary retinopathy evidenced by hyperpigmentation on fundus photography, superior temporal visual field defect, centripetal reduction, interruption in ellipsoid band, and hyperreflective deposits on macular SD-OCT
Cardiac conduction abnormalities, specifically intermittent first-degree atrioventricular block and partial second-degree type I atrioventricular block on 24-h ambulatory ECG
History of growth retardation, dizziness, and fatigue

remaining_uncertainties: Specific genetic abnormality (e.g., mitochondrial DNA deletion) identified by gene detection
Presence or absence of cerebellar ataxia
